newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL secondaries add to gains, blue chips slip.
newsitem.headline: KL secondaries add to gains, blue chips slip.

text.p: Persistent retail buying chased Kuala Lumpur secondary stocks higher, but blue chips continued to fade amid a lack of institutional interest.
The blue chip-focused Composite Index fell 1.05 points to 1,104.28, while the Second Board index ended up 6.60 points to 560.99.

Stocks stayed mixed throughout that day after opening firmer. "It's the same old story," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities. "The Second Board's testing new highs, while the Composite Index is trying not to dip."
The Second Board index, which focuses on small-capitalisation counters, surged to a new intraday high of 565.59 earlier in the session.
News that Malaysia's gross domestic product grew 8.4 percent in the second quarter this year versus 8.3 percent in the previous quarter was ignored by the market.
"Everything is as expected," said one institutional dealer with a bank-linked brokerage firm. "We're having growth. It's slow, but it's still there."
By the close, over 240 million shares had changed hands, and gainers led losers by 318 to 223.
